events.headline: US-Iran diplomacy stalls: Rubio demands Iran's UN delegation leave the US after ceasefire-proposal talks break down; Trump denies reports he was ready to offer Tehran sanctions relief, keeping Middle East tensions elevated

Crude slipped to ~$92.63/bbl (WTI) on Oct 2, down slightly, but supply stays tight (Gulf output ~5M bpd below pre-war levels amid Hormuz disruption); OPEC+ meets Oct 4 and is expected to hold November quotas steady

China's rare-earth/lithium-battery export-control suspension (in place since the Xi-Trump Busan meeting) remains set to expire Nov 10, 2026, with China having separately added US rare-earth firms (MP Materials, USA Rare Earth) to its control list this year, keeping supply-chain risk elevated

Morgan Stanley reinstated Nvidia as its semiconductor 'Top Pick' after meetings with CEO Jensen Huang and CFO Colette Kress; Broadcom's banking syndicate is reportedly gathering $60B in fresh financing for AI chips/infrastructure benefiting Anthropic and others
Intel shares surged over 11% as Meta's Muse AI agent boosted expectations for CPU-heavy, agentic AI workloads in data centers, reinforcing Intel's server-CPU growth story
Fed Chair Warsh remains hawkish with core PCE inflation at 3.3% (up from 3.0% in Dec 2025); fixed-income markets are now pricing back-to-back rate hikes at the Oct 28 and December 2026 FOMC meetings
